newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESCO Holdings chosen to buy Estonian Shipping.
newsitem.headline: ESCO Holdings chosen to buy Estonian Shipping.

text.p: The Estonian Privatisation Agency said on Wednesday it had chosen ESCO Holdings to take a 70 percent stake in the Estonian Shipping company.
A privatisation agency official told a news conference it had chosen ESCO over another consortium, Arbonale, to buy the stake in the shipping company, one of Estonia's leading state-run companies.
ESCO Holdings made a 700 million kroon ($51 million) bid for the shipping company and has said it will invest 3.1 billion kroons.
ESCO is held 50 percent by Norwegian Tschudi & Eitzen, 12 percent by Uhisinvesteeringud, the investment arm of Uhispank, and 10 percent by U.S. Stanton Capital.
Investment house Baltic Cresco has 10 percent, the management of Estonian Shipping another 10 percent and eight percent belongs to Estonian food production company EPEKS.
Arbonale bid 612 million kroons and proposed investing 3.55 billion kroons in the company.

Arbonale was formed by investment banks Talinvest and Hansa Investments, Estonian oil fuel terminal N-Terminaal, Norwegian shipper Navigator, Japanese investment bank Nomura and Hong Kong shipper Jinhui Shipping and Transportation Ltd.
